title: Automatic metrics sanitizer and Grafana dashboard ownership migration
author: Asha Mehta
ci_checks: e2e: private-installer-canary — pass (flaky on first run, rerun passed)
description: Problem: Customer installs occasionally surface metric label values that include tenant identifiers or user-created labels which may be considered PII or destabilize prometheus label cardinality. In addition, upgrades that move dashboards from a shared Grafana folder into tenant-specific folders require a repeatable migration that preserves ownership and panel links but avoids double-posting during a rollback. Motivation: Provide an automated, opinionated safe-path for private installs to (1) sanitize metric label values before they are scraped/ingested and (2) perform an atomic dashboard migration with a snapshotter that can be rolled back cleanly. This PR implements: 1) metrics-sanitizer sidecar + Prometheus relabeling profiles: a small Go sidecar (pkg/metrics/sanitizer) that rewrites configured label keys via allowlist/replace rules before metrics are forwarded to remote write or scraped by Prometheus. The sanitizer is optional and controlled by Helm values: observability.metricsSanitizer.enabled and observability.metricsSanitizer.rules (regex replace). 2) terraform module param: monitoring->enable_metrics_sanitizer boolean and monitoring->sanitizer_rules_map so customers can configure rules at install-time. 3) Grafana folder snapshotter operator (helm hook + small job) that: - creates tenant folders if missing - exports dashboards from the shared folder into tenant folders with metadata indicating migration version - writes a migration manifest to the cluster (ConfigMap) used by the installer to detect partial migrations and drive idempotent retries 4) upgrade/rollback playbook additions (docs/installer/upgrade-playbooks/observability-migration.md) with exact kubectl/helm steps and an automated dry-run flag for the snapshotter. 5) E2E tests and integration harness updates: added canary scenario that deploys sanitizer rules and validates metric label rewriting as well as dashboard import idempotency. Checklist (what I ran locally / in canary): - unit tests: pkg/metrics (go test) - integration: e2e private-installer canary against a k3s cluster - helm lint and template validation - tf plan for terraform/module changes - dry-run migration and full migration exercise - rollback simulation (run snapshotter revert path) Related work: ENG-7843 (metric governance), ENG-7899 (dashboard migration framework), SUP-9124 (customer case where tenant-id leaked into kafka consumer metrics). Notes on risk and behavior: - The sanitizer runs as an opt-in sidecar. If enabled for an install, it rewrites labels before Prometheus sees them; this changes metric cardinality and may affect alert thresholds — upgrade notes include recommended evaluation steps. - The Grafana snapshotter is additive by default and writes a migration manifest; rollback path removes migrated dashboards and restores pointers to shared folder (playbook included). - Backwards compatibility: installs that do not enable these features see no runtime changes. How to review: focus on the sanitizer rules engine safety (pkg/metrics/sanitizer; tests cover regex escapes), TF module variable naming and defaults (terraform/modules/monitoring/variables.tf), and the migration manifest format (docs describe JSON schema).

release_notes: Opt-in metrics sanitizer sidecar for private installs (helm/terraform controlled). Grafana dashboard snapshotter for safe tenant migration during upgrades. Includes upgrade/rollback playbook and e2e canary tests.
migration_plan: 1) Dry-run: enable snapshotter with --dry-run to generate migration manifest in a canary cluster. 2) Enable metricsSanitizer.rules with narrow rule set and validate in canary for 72h. 3) Run full migration with snapshotter and verify dashboards in tenant folders. 4) If issues: follow rollback steps in docs which remove migrated dashboards and point tenant consumers back to shared folder; apply Terraform to set enable_metrics_sanitizer=false and redeploy helm chart. 5) For production installations, run a phased rollout across tenants using canary tenant label selectors (instructions included in docs).
